title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77562-5

Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise safe energy storage but suffer from dendrites and side reactions. Here, authors engineer a zwitterionic fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte to suppress these issues, enabling durable, dendrite free, Ah-level pouch cells.

title: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78166-9

Here, Pulliam and colleagues characterize the metabolites encoded by tumor-inhabiting microbes and their potential role in cancer pathology.

title: Structural basis of voltage gating in a partially activated K<sup>+</sup> channel
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78089-5

The process by which the voltage sensor electromechanically couples to the pore in K+ channels is not fully understood. A cryo-EM structure of a partially activated state, together with computational modeling and MD simulations, clarifies the mechanistic basis for electromechanical coupling.

title: Parasitological efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Africa
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78189-2

In this study, the authors show that post-treatment desethylamodiaquine concentration is the primary pharmacokinetic determinant of protection against malaria infection in African children who are given sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention, with little apparent effect from sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.

title: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77955-6

Plant sensors are emerging as key tools for precision agriculture, yet continuous monitoring of biomarkers in plant biofluids remains underdeveloped. Here, the authors introduce PlantIonics, a wearable microfluidic electrochemical platform for multiplexed, in situ analysis of guttation fluid. The system enables continuous, noninvasive monitoring of stress-associated plant physiological and metabolic responses under changing environmental conditions.

title: Chromosome-scale assembly of yeast genomes using enzyme-free, dense optical genome mapping
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78211-7

Optical genome mapping (OGM) provides long-range genomic information but relies on sparse enzymatic labeling that restricts resolution in poorly labeled or structurally complex regions. Here the authors assemble yeast genomes at chromosome scale using dense OGM, resolving large repetitive regions.

title: Cross-border electricity tariffs undermine power system efficiency, decarbonization and reliability in North America
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77773-w

Analysis of a decade of New York power-market data and simulations shows that tariffs on Canadian electricity imports could raise prices and emissions, diminish economic benefits, and weaken grid reliability during peak demand and extreme weather.

title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77925-y

In this exploratory randomized trial, the monoclonal antibody AER002 was safe but did not improve clinical or biomarker outcomes in Long COVID. Post-hoc findings suggest baseline antibody levels and drug exposure may inform future studies.
